question: Your team runs Claude Code in the CI/CD pipeline for several workloads. To cut costs, a lead proposes moving one workload to the Message Batches API. This API gives 50% cost savings, but processing can take up to 24 hours and has no guaranteed latency SLA. Which workload is the best fit for the Message Batches API?

options.text: Pull request feedback that developers wait for before they continue to edit and push their next commit.
options.reason: Developers wait for this feedback, so the workflow is blocking, and the guide says batch processing is inappropriate for blocking workflows.

options.text: Nightly test case generation for code merged during the day, with results that developers review the next morning.
options.reason: This workload is non-blocking and latency-tolerant, and the guide names nightly test generation as appropriate for batch processing.

options.text: The pre-merge code review check that must finish before a developer is allowed to merge a pull request.
options.reason: A pre-merge check is a blocking workflow, and the guide says it belongs on the synchronous API because batch processing has no guaranteed latency SLA.

options.text: The automated review that the deployment pipeline must complete before it releases an urgent hotfix to production.
options.reason: The release waits on this review, so the workflow is blocking and needs the synchronous API rather than a batch with up to 24 hours of processing.
